root_cause_criterion.criterion: Before the `H5G_CACHED_STAB` arm decodes the two cached addresses, the required scratch span `2 * H5F_SIZEOF_ADDR(f)` must fit within `H5G_SIZEOF_SCRATCH`. Otherwise the second `H5F_addr_decode()` consumes bytes beyond the fixed 16-byte scratch area attached to the root entry.
root_cause_criterion.description: The vulnerable witness reaches the cached-STAB arm with `H5F_SIZEOF_ADDR(f) == 16`, so the arm demands 32 scratch bytes while the format provides only `H5G_SIZEOF_SCRATCH == 16`. The authoritative fixed program guards this obligation on the original input and genuinely re-executes the protected second decode on the nearest safe boundary perturbation `sizeof_addr_boundary_8_cached_stab`, where `bytes_needed == scratch_bytes == 16`.
root_cause_criterion.verification_note: The fixed original remains guarded at this site; differential verification therefore uses the adjacent genuine witness case `sizeof_addr_boundary_8_cached_stab`, which reduces only the address-width byte to the boundary value 8 and rewrites the newly-shifted cache-type word back to `H5G_CACHED_STAB` so the same protected decode path still executes.

nodes.state: Immediately before the second cached-STAB address decode, `*pp` is already equal to the caller's one-past-end superblock image pointer `(const uint8_t *)_image + len`, so the second decode begins exactly at the first byte beyond the heap-backed image.

At the AddressSanitizer read site `c = *(*pp)++`, `*pp` is still the exact pointer passed into the second cached-STAB decode, so the sink dereferences the same one-past-end address selected by `H5G_ent_decode()`.

edges.relation: The caller's superblock image-end pointer `(const uint8_t *)_image + len` is the same pointer value observed as `*pp` immediately before `H5G_ent_decode()` issues the second cached-STAB address decode.
The exact pointer handed to the second `H5F_addr_decode()` call is passed unchanged into `H5F_addr_decode_len()` and becomes the `*pp` byte-read operand at the sink.
